items.stem: A car enters a corner and the front tyres lose grip first, so the car runs wide of the intended line. This behaviour is called:

options.rationale: Oversteer is when the rear loses grip first and the tail slides out.
When the front loses grip first and the car runs wide, the vehicle is understeering.
Neutral steer is balanced front and rear grip loss, not running wide.
Weight transfer is a cause of grip changes, not the name of this handling state.

items.explanation: When the front loses grip first and the car runs wide, the vehicle is understeering.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: What does the tyre friction circle primarily illustrate?

options.text: That tyre grip is unlimited in all directions
options.rationale: The whole point of the circle is that grip is limited.

options.text: That the combined longitudinal and lateral force a tyre can produce is limited by a finite total grip
options.rationale: The friction circle shows that braking and cornering forces share one finite grip budget.

options.text: That tyres never generate lateral force
options.rationale: Tyres generate lateral force when cornering; the circle bounds it.

options.text: That tyre temperature has no effect on grip
options.rationale: The circle is about force limits, and temperature does affect grip.

items.explanation: The friction circle shows that braking and cornering forces share one finite grip budget.

items.stem: An engineer wants to reduce mid-corner understeer in a front-engined car. Select TWO changes that typically shift the balance away from understeer.

options.rationale: A softer front bar increases front grip relative to rear, reducing understeer.
A stiffer rear bar reduces rear grip relative to front, shifting balance toward neutral or oversteer.
A stiffer front bar reduces front grip and increases understeer.

options.text: Increase front tyre pressures far above the optimum
options.rationale: Over-inflating the fronts reduces their contact grip and worsens understeer.

options.text: Add ballast over the front axle
options.rationale: More front mass generally increases understeer, not reduce it.

items.explanation: A softer front bar increases front grip relative to rear, reducing understeer.
